answer: Divergent-Challenge Identity Quota. Each identity must sign a random challenge derived from its own past actions; because clones cannot diverge, copying a history forces identical answers, so the system caps how many identities can share one trajectory. An attacker cloning one agent pays fresh voyage costs for every copy, since each must build a distinct trajectory to pass. Any collision flags a signal of duplication and throttles the batch. Honest agents navigate the reef of quota checks cheaply, while mass cloning multiplies storage and signing overhead linearly per identity.
